column5: NC State Appendix E: row covers and low tunnels can offer 4 to 5 F of frost protection and screen out some insects and diseases, though pests already present can be trapped underneath; vent by slitting the top in advance when temperatures under the cover will pass 90 F for several hours. Confirms the module 1 figure currently tagged 'unverified'.

NC State Appendix E cold frames: sun is the only heat source; site facing south or south-east on a slight slope, with a wall or hedge to the north; sinking the frame helps insulate it; keep it no wider than 4 to 5 feet to reach across; never build it from wood treated with CCA, creosote or pentachlorophenol, which harm plants, and prefer a decay-resistant wood such as cedar; on a cold snap cover with sacks of leaves, blankets or tarps, or stack straw bales; ventilation matters most on clear sunny days in late winter, spring and early autumn, closing the sash early enough to keep heat for the evening; a hot bed adds heat from cables or 18 inches of fresh horse manure under 6 inches of soil.

NC State Appendix E structures: small greenhouses fluctuate in temperature faster than large ones because the air volume is small, so an open door gains or loses a lot of heat; plastic pipe frames are generally inadequate for snow and wind loads; tempered glass is two to three times stronger than ordinary glass; utility polythene lasts about a year, greenhouse-grade UV-stabilised film 12 to 18 months, copolymers two to three years; poor fibreglass discolours and loses light.

NC State Appendix E: all gas, oil and wood-burning heaters must be vented outside, and unvented propane or kerosene heaters are not recommended; circulation fans at one quarter of the air volume per minute, run continuously in winter and switched off in summer when venting; summer ventilation of 1 to 1.5 air changes a minute, winter 20 to 30% of one change; sensors shaded, at plant height, in moving air. Matches modules 1 and 5.

NC State Appendix E: season extenders can give warm-season crops such as tomatoes and cucumbers as much as a month's head start in spring or a month's extension in autumn, and greens can be harvested all winter with the right conditions; high tunnels mainly raise temperatures a few degrees each day over several weeks rather than giving strong frost protection.
